correctness.rationale: For a monotone self-map of a finite tree order, the stable image supports an order automorphism. Its action on maximal elements is faithful because maximal-descendant sets distinguish incomparable points and principal-ideal cardinality distinguishes comparable points; its maximal set has size at most the ambient number of leaves. Therefore any eventual preimage period divides an order of a permutation of at most that many letters. The prime-power assignment inequality gives the necessary leaf budget, and permuting leaves while mapping interior points to the root gives every admissible period. The full symbolic proof covers all finite sizes. The packaged finite checker passed 168,950 valuations on all 5,430 monotone self-maps of 34 increasing-parent rooted-tree representations through five vertices.

value.rationale: In finite Alexandrov temporal model checking, exact global truth-set recurrence can be much longer than any single path and depends on the finite world graph. The theorem replaces the naive point-count period bound by a sharp shape-invariant leaf-budget spectrum for an important rooted tree class, with exact arithmetical gaps and constructive attainment on every fixed tree. The surprising period six with five leaves and the sharp diamond obstruction illustrate nontrivial behavior. It does not rest on a tiny numerical recomputation or on the already-known Landau sequence.
